history.dynasty: None (folk tradition; present temple built by the Hindu Jat king Jawahar Singh of Bharatpur)
history.summary: The famous Sheetla Mata Mandir of Gurugram is dedicated to Kripi/Kirpai, also called Lalitha - the wife of Guru Dronacharya (Mahabharata). According to legend she lived in Keshopur village (now Delhi) and devoted herself to nursing children suffering from smallpox; after her death she was deified as Mata Sheetla (Sanskrit 'the one who cools') or Mata Masani, the goddess of smallpox. A few centuries ago Chaudhari Singh Ram (alias Singha Bhagat), a fief-holder of Gurgaon village, is said to have dreamed the goddess asking to be brought from Keshopur to Gurgaon; he installed her there. The present temple was built in the 18th century by Maharaja Jawahar Singh of Bharatpur as thanksgiving after a victory over the Mughals. The temple is managed by the Shree Mata Sheetla Devi Shrine Board, constituted under the Shri Mata Sheetla Devi Shrine Board Act, 1991. Note: one exam-prep site calls it 'one of the nine Shaktipeeths' - this is NOT one of the classical Shakti Peethas; treat as a local devotional claim (verify).

name: Sheetla Mata Mandir
town_description: Gurugram (formerly Gurgaon) is a major satellite city of Delhi in Haryana's National Capital Region. Its name derives from Guru Dronacharya, whose ashram is traditionally placed here. It is one of India's biggest IT, finance and startup hubs - the 'Millennium City'. The Sheetla Mata Mandir in old Gurugram is the city's kuldevi (guardian deity) shrine and one of the busiest pilgrimage sites in the NCR, drawing huge crowds during Navratri fairs.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi - about 20-25 km (verify).
travel.road: On Sheetla Mata Road in old Gurugram, off Old Delhi Road; connected via NH-48 (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Navratri fairs (March-April and September-October) draw the largest crowds - visit on a non-festival weekday to avoid them.
